english: Do you have a baby bed?
japanese: ベビーベッドって、ありますか？
note: tte softens it — you sound like you're wondering, not demanding

english: Could we have a high chair for the meal?
japanese: お食事のとき、ベビーチェアをお願いできますか？
romaji: o-shokuji no toki, bebī chea o onegai dekimasu ka?
note: Say this before mealtime at the ryokan, not mid-seating

english: Could I have some hot water?
japanese: お湯をいただけますか？
note: For warming milk or formula

english: Could we have a few more towels?
japanese: タオルをもう少しいただけますか？
romaji: taoru o mō sukoshi itadakemasu ka?
note: mō sukoshi = a little more — polite, not greedy-sounding

english: Do you have a yukata for children?
japanese: 子ども用の浴衣はありますか？
romaji: kodomo-yō no yukata wa arimasu ka?
note: Most ryokans have these but may not set them out automatically

english: Until what time can we use the large bath?
japanese: 大浴場は何時まで使えますか？
romaji: daiyokujō wa nanji made tsukaemasu ka?
note: Ask on arrival at Yoshiike and Kawane Onsen

english: Do you have a private (family) bath?
japanese: 貸切風呂はありますか？
note: The most useful onsen question with a toddler — sidesteps shared-bath rules. Often needs booking at check-in, sometimes for a fee

english: Two adults, one child — could we have a high chair?
japanese: 大人二人と、子ども一人なんですが、ベビーチェアをお願いできますか？
romaji: otona futari to, kodomo hitori nan desu ga, bebī chea o onegai dekimasu ka?
note: nan desu ga sets context first, then makes the request

english: Do you have a children's menu?
japanese: お子様メニューはありますか？
note: o-ko-sama is the restaurant-level polite word for child

english: A small plate for sharing, please
japanese: 取り分け用のお皿をお願いします
romaji: torikawake-yō no o-sara o onegai shimasu
note: You'll want this at nearly every meal. Say o-sara futatsu for two plates

japanese: 子ども用の食器はありますか？
romaji: kodomo-yō no shokki wa arimasu ka?
note: shokki covers plates, bowls and cutlery. Swap in: o-sara (plate), o-wan (bowl), supūn (spoon), fōku (fork), koppu (cup)
Negative question = more natural than asking 'is this spicy?' directly

japanese: お会計をお願いします
note: More natural than just saying kaikei alone

english: I'd like to get here… [show map]
japanese: ここに行きたいんですが
romaji: koko ni ikitai n desu ga
note: Trail off — the unfinished ga implies 'can you help?'
Casual iranai works too; daijōbu desu is smoothest at a conbini
Toire is universally understood
Useful habit — e.g. Kosaku in Kawaguchiko is cash-only

japanese: レギュラー、満タンでお願いします
note: For full-service stations. Many are self-serve (セルフ). Return the rental full
For reporting a problem. To ASK if you can use one: ETC kādo wa tsukaemasu ka?

japanese: ベビーカー置き場はどこですか？
romaji: bebīkā okiba wa doko desu ka?
note: okiba = storage spot — literally 'place for placing'

english: What's the minimum age for this ride?
japanese: このアトラクションは何歳から乗れますか？
romaji: kono atorakushon wa nansai kara noremasu ka?

note: The most formal 'yes, I'll do it'. Your request has been accepted
Expect this before they fetch something or make a call
gozaimasu is the formal service version of arimasu — same meaning

english: I'm very sorry — we don't have that
note: A deep apology. After a request, this means no

japanese: ただいまお持ちします
note: Said after you've requested something — it's on its way

english: Sorry to have kept you waiting
note: A reflex every time staff return to you — not an apology for a real wait
Heard when being led to a table — just follow

japanese: ご予約はございますか？
note: First thing you'll hear at any mid-range restaurant
Hold up fingers if needed. nan-nin is the less formal version

replyList.r: otona futari to, kodomo hitori desu

japanese: ご注文はお決まりですか？
note: The waiter's cue that they're ready to take your order

japanese: お名前をお聞かせください
note: Heard at ryokan check-in — have your booking name ready

japanese: ただいま満席でございます
note: Restaurant is full. Ask the wait time, or bow and move on

english: Do you have a point card?
japanese: ポイントカードはお持ちですか？
romaji: pointo kādo wa o-mochi desu ka?
note: Asked at nearly every conbini and chain store

japanese: お子さんは何歳ですか？
note: Softer variant: o-ikutsu desu ka. Ages use -sai
Often just otoko no ko? with rising tone

japanese: おむつは取れていますか？
note: Asked at onsen and pools — many baths require children to be toilet-trained

romaji: sumimasen, mada wakarimasen. eigo de onegai dekimasu ka?
